metadata.title: ITER-31 Second-Dataset Feasibility Comparison
metadata.author: Antigravity Research Team
metadata.primary_benchmark: JIGSAWS (3 tasks, 103 trials, 8 subjects, 76D kinematics, 30 Hz nominal sync)

SurgSync.name: SurgSync
SurgSync.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2026)
SurgSync.authors: Haoying Zhou, Chang Liu, Yimeng Wu, Junlin Wu, Zijian Wu, Yu Chung Lee, Sara Martuscelli, Septimiu E. Salcudean, Gregory S. Fischer, Peter Kazanzides
SurgSync.public_availability: Publicly hosted on Hugging Face and GitHub; open access without gated institutional approval
SurgSync.license: Open research use (MIT / Apache 2.0 compatible open-source license for toolbox and dataset)
SurgSync.hardware_platform: da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK Classic and dVRK-Si) with modern chip-on-tip 1080p stereo endoscope and capacitive contact sensing
SurgSync.recording_conditions: Ex-vivo tissue (chicken breast, beef, pork) and anatomical phantoms within Intuitive abdominal dome

modalities.video: Stereo 1080p (Left/Right) at 10-30 FPS, modern chip-on-tip endoscope
modalities.kinematics: 14D synchronized feature vectors (6D Cartesian position, 6D measured linear/angular velocity, 2D gripper angle) + raw dVRK ROS joint/setpoint topics
modalities.contact_sensing: Capacitive contact ground-truth sensor (Arduino/dVRK digital input)
modalities.synchronization_mechanism: Dual-mode hardware/software synchronized recorders (online-matching: 6.36 +/- 4.72 ms latency; offline-matching: 1.35 +/- 0.81 ms latency at 10 Hz)

annotation_granularity.gesture_taxonomy: 14-class surgical gesture taxonomy adhering directly to the JIGSAWS taxonomy (G1-G14)
annotation_granularity.skill_assessment: Global Rating Score (GRS, 6-30 scale across 6 domains)
annotation_granularity.trial_level_breakdown: 43 validated instances across 8 users split into discrete suturing and knot-tying sequences

SurgSync.subject_independent_splits: Supported (8 human subjects with distinct skill levels: Novice, Intermediate, Expert; 4-fold user-stratified cross-validation protocol published)

pipeline_compatibility.visual_encoder: Directly compatible with SurgMotion-L (requires 16-frame tubelet extraction on 1080p frames downsampled to 224x224)
pipeline_compatibility.kinematics_head: Directly compatible with KinematicsGRU (14D Cartesian/velocity features map 1-to-1 to subset of JIGSAWS kinematics)
pipeline_compatibility.fusion_architecture: Directly compatible with AdaptiveReliabilityFusion and ReliabilityGate
pipeline_compatibility.missing_modality_robustness: Directly compatible with availability mask [a_v, a_k] and continuous feature noise stress testing

feasibility_assessment.key_strengths: Same dVRK robotic platform, identical JIGSAWS 14-gesture taxonomy for suturing/knot tying, rigorous sub-7ms time synchronization, open Hugging Face access, modern high-fidelity endoscope
feasibility_assessment.primary_risks: 1080p video extraction requires mentor GPU compute for SurgMotion caching; kinematic dimensionality is 14D (Cartesian) vs 76D (full joint/transform)

ROSMAG40.name: ROSMAG40 (subset of ROSMA)
ROSMAG40.authors: Irene Rivas-Blanco, Carmen Lopez-Casado, Juan Maria Herrera-Lopez, Jose Cabrera Villa, Carlos J. Perez-del-Pulgar

modalities.kinematics: High-frequency PSM and MTM joint kinematics

annotation_granularity.gesture_taxonomy: Two-level custom taxonomy: Maneuver Descriptors (MD, high-level) and Fine-Grained Descriptors (FGD, basic actions: touch, grasp, translate, release)
annotation_granularity.jigsaws_alignment: Incompatible with JIGSAWS G1-G15 taxonomy (different tasks, different movement semantics)

ROSMAG40.subject_independent_splits: Limited documentation on user identity splits across the 22 videos

pipeline_compatibility.kinematics_head: Requires re-engineering kinematic parser for ROSMA custom format
pipeline_compatibility.fusion_architecture: Compatible, but requires training a new classifier head from scratch

feasibility_assessment.key_strengths: Public Zenodo download with CC-BY 4.0 license; dVRK platform
feasibility_assessment.primary_risks: Only 22 trials; non-surgical tasks (post/sleeve, wire chaser); gesture labels completely incompatible with JIGSAWS; small sample size limits statistical generalization

MISAW.name: MISAW (MIcro-Surgical Anastomose Workflow)
MISAW.venue: MICCAI 2020 Endoscopic Vision Challenge / Medical Image Analysis
MISAW.authors: Arnaud Huaulme et al. (Challenge Organizing Committee)
MISAW.public_availability: Gated access via Sage Bionetworks Synapse (requires user registration and challenge terms agreement)
MISAW.license: Challenge-specific academic research agreement / CC-BY-NC 4.0 for derivatives
MISAW.hardware_platform: Custom master-slave micro-surgical robotic platform (University of Tokyo) + high-resolution stereo operating microscope
MISAW.recording_conditions: Micro-vascular anastomosis on artificial silicone blood vessels (0.7 mm diameter)

modalities.video: Stereoscopic surgical microscope video at 30 Hz
modalities.kinematics: Motor and joint encoder trajectories from Tokyo micro-surgical robot at 30 Hz

annotation_granularity.gesture_taxonomy: Hierarchical workflow: Phases, Steps, and Activities (<verb, instrument, target> triplets)
annotation_granularity.jigsaws_alignment: Zero overlap with JIGSAWS gesture classes (micro-surgical triplet grammar vs macro-surgical gesture segments)

pipeline_compatibility.kinematics_head: Incompatible with 76D da Vinci kinematics (requires custom parser for micro-robot coordinates)
pipeline_compatibility.fusion_architecture: Requires rewriting classification heads for triplet prediction rather than gesture recognition

feasibility_assessment.key_strengths: Real micro-surgical procedure; 30 Hz synchronized video and kinematics
feasibility_assessment.primary_risks: Gated Synapse platform access; micro-surgical robot (not da Vinci); triplet workflow annotations incompatible with our gesture recognition architecture; substantial re-engineering required

direct_cross_dataset_transfer.rationale: Direct zero-shot transfer of JIGSAWS-trained gesture models to a second dataset is unfeasible for ROSMAG40 and MISAW due to conflicting label taxonomies. Even for SurgSync, sensor coordinate frames (14D Cartesian vs 76D joint/transform) prevent zero-shot kinematics transfer without domain re-projection.

independent_within_dataset_evaluation.rationale: Training and evaluating AdaptiveReliabilityFusion within SurgSync (Suturing and Knot Tying tasks) under identical LOUO protocol independently validates the multimodal hypothesis on modern ex-vivo robotic surgery data.

cross_dataset_robustness_validation.rationale: Benchmarking whether the ReliabilityGate's noise mitigation and single-modality fallback generalize to SurgSync proves that reliability-aware fusion is a general principle rather than a JIGSAWS-specific artifact.

recommended_pilot.estimated_training_time: ~45 minutes for 4-fold CV on primary laptop
